Classification: Low Clan

Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} are wanderers, trusted by almost none, blamed for spreading vice and discord wherever they travel. European @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} trace their lineage to migrations from lands beyond Persia as far back as Alexander the Great, splitting into several distinct jati (castes) scattered across Europe, Africa and the Middle East; a newer wave claims a different, grander origin and offers little explanation of the discrepancy. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} are fiercely loyal to their own jati — a wronged Ravnos can expect vengeance from sire, fellow childer, and progeny alike — which makes princes wary of punishing them despite their reputation. Many masquerade as members of other clans to move more freely; others operate openly as traders, messengers, mercenaries or spies.

Disciplines: Animalism, Chimerstry, Fortitude

Advantage: Ravnos start with one free Trait of Street or Transportation Influence and an associated Ability Trait of Larceny or Subterfuge. Local justice tends to overlook minor thefts and deceptions by traveling Ravnos, though such leniency expects them to move on quickly.

Disadvantage: All Ravnos suffer a compulsive disorder tied to a vice chosen at character creation (pride, lust, greed, theft, confidence schemes, etc.). Presented with an opportunity to indulge it, a Ravnos cannot refuse unless she wins a Self-Control/Instinct Challenge (difficulty three Traits); if no opportunity arises during a session, she must contrive one.

Organization: Disjointed and distrustful even of each other; Eastern and Western Ravnos factions oppose one another, though bonds of family and caste run deep.

Suggested Viae: Many follow Sin or Humanity. Traditionalists follow the Road of Paradox.
